chunks.text:
Procurement Policy > Overview > Purpose and scope

This policy establishes the framework for procurement activities to ensure that the organization consistently achieves value for money. It promotes transparent, competitive, and standardized processes, while supporting efficient, ethical, and commercially sound procurement practices. It applies to all procurement of goods, works, and services undertaken by Nebras.

Procurement Policy > Overview > Purpose and scope > Excluded from scope

- Employment-related contracts. - Low-value purchases below defined thresholds (e.g. petty cash or corporate card use). - Utility services (e.g. electricity, water, telecommunications). - Real estate transactions (e.g. office leases, land acquisition). - Insurance policies (e.g. medical, asset, liability coverage).

Procurement Policy > Principles & provisions > Key principles and general provisions > Key procurement principles

- Value for money — the Procurement function MUST consider all options and develop strategies that achieve the most advantageous combination of total cost, quality, and sustainability on a case-by-case basis. - Fair and equal competition — all processes MUST be open, transparent, and competitive; bidders shall be treated equally and provided with the same information simultaneously. - Conflict of interest and ethical conduct — personnel MUST adhere to the HR Policy and Code of Conduct, avoid real or perceived conflicts of interest, reject gifts, bribery, corruption, or favouritism, and MUST NOT disclose bid or contract details to unauthorized parties. - Proportionality — the procurement process MUST be proportionate to the size and nature of the requirement, avoiding unnecessary burdens on Nebras and bidders. - Protecting the interests of Nebras — evaluate risks, maintain comprehensive records, operate within the Delegation of Authority (DoA), require bidders to sign NDAs before receiving tender documents, and comply with applicable UAE laws.

Procurement Policy > Principles & provisions > Key principles and general provisions > General provisions

- Procurement shall be conducted in a fair, transparent, and competitive manner. - Splitting procurement requirements to bypass approval thresholds is strictly prohibited. - Procurement activities MUST comply with applicable UAE laws and local content requirements. - All procurement MUST be supported by an approved budget and relevant approvals as per the DoA. - A valid contract or purchase order MUST be issued before engaging any supplier. - Nebras reserves the right to reject invoices submitted without a valid agreement.

Procurement Policy > Governance & Committee > Dual control and the Procurement Committee

The Procurement Committee shall be appointed upon the approval of the CEO and comprises a Chairperson, Secretary, Permanent Members, Advisory Members, and Invitee Members as required. Its detailed role, responsibilities, composition, and operating procedures are defined in the Procurement Committee Charter, which shall be reviewed and updated annually.

chunks.text:
Procurement Policy > Governance & Committee > Dual control and the Procurement Committee > The Committee provides oversight of

- Procurement transactions exceeding AED 500,000. - Contract variations greater than 20% of an existing contract. - Single or sole source procurement requests. - Contract renewal and termination requests. The Procurement Committee finalizes evaluation for RFP/RFQs under AED 3 million. Anything above AED 3 million in value — or other values as per the defined DoA — is referred to the CBUAE’s Procurement Committee.

chunks.text:
Procurement Policy > Methods & thresholds > Procurement methods and value thresholds > Direct procurement

- Petty cash — low-value purchases below AED 1,000 for immediate and incidental needs, administered by the Finance Department and supported by valid receipts. - Corporate card — low-value purchases from AED 1,000 to AED 5,000, issued and controlled by the Finance Department, with the Procurement Manager determining card versus purchase order. - Direct purchase order — low-risk, low-value purchases from AED 5,001 up to AED 50,000, supported by a valid Purchase Requisition and necessary technical approvals.

Procurement Policy > Methods & thresholds > Procurement methods and value thresholds > Competitive procurement

- RFQ — for standard, low-complexity goods with clearly defined specifications, valued above AED 50,000 to below AED 1,000,000. - RFP — for medium-complexity procurements above AED 50,000 to below AED 1,000,000, where both technical and commercial evaluations are necessary; a minimum of three proposals shall be sought from qualified vendors. - Tender — for high-value and complex procurements from AED 1,000,000, using a sealed-envelope process with a minimum of three sealed bids from qualified vendors. For procurements valued at AED 500,000 and above, Procurement Committee approval shall be required prior to Delegation of Authority (DOA) approval. Procurement Policy > Tender lifecycle > From requisition to award

The End-User raises a Purchase Requisition (PR) aligned to the approved budget, with clear scope of work, specifications, BOQ, quantities, and the correct asset, material, or service code. PRs that split values to bypass approval limits are strictly prohibited. The Bidders List is drawn from the Approved Vendor list, an End-User proposed bidders list, or the prequalification process. A minimum of three bids shall be sought from qualified vendors. Opening follows a structured, two-stage process: technical submissions are accessed first for evaluation, and commercial submissions remain restricted until the technical evaluation is formally completed and approved. Conducted against predefined, approved technical criteria by End-Users and assigned cross-department members, with all pricing information excluded. A structured Post-Tender Clarification (PTC) may be initiated prior to commercial opening. Only the commercial submissions of technically qualified bidders are opened. The commercial evaluation is conducted exclusively by the Procurement Department, without involvement from the technical team or other departments. Negotiation may be authorized with the lowest or multiple bidders. The best evaluated offer is submitted for Procurement Committee review and endorsement, followed by final approval in line with the DOA. The award is issued through a signed Letter of Award (LOA) in accordance with the DOA. All unsuccessful bidders receive a formal regret notification in writing. - Tender Guarantee — 1% of the total bid value, in the form of a bank guarantee or security cheque, determined case-by-case; returned to unsuccessful bidders following contract award. - Performance Guarantee — 10% of the total contract value from the successful supplier. A supplier may request to deduct an amount from payable invoices as an alternative, subject to Procurement Committee approval.

Procurement Policy > Special arrangements > Non-competitive and framework arrangements

- Single / sole source — a supplier may be selected without competition where goods or services are available from only one source, an officially authorized distributor exists, or the End-User relies on proven performance with written justification. All such requests MUST be justified, submitted to the Procurement Committee for endorsement, documented, and subject to periodic audit review. - Purchase Order variation / Change Request — a variation of 20% or less is reviewed and endorsed by the Procurement Manager prior to final DOA approval; a variation above 20% MUST be submitted to the Procurement Committee. - Emergency procurement — used only where there is an immediate threat to health, safety, operations, or reputation; each request MUST be justified by the requesting Business Unit and approved per the DoA. - Blanket Agreement — established for recurring procurement of goods where exact quantities are uncertain but anticipated over a defined period, at fixed pricing. - Framework Agreement — used for recurring procurement of services with uncertain quantities or timing; it MUST define the contract period, scope, and pricing. - Special procurement — for Marketing Events, Brand Campaigns, and CSR Sponsorships, a tailored approach evaluates proposals on creativity, strategic alignment, execution capability, and value for money. A minimum of three proposals shall be solicited, except for CSR sponsorships, and all such procurements MUST have pre-approved budgets.

Procurement Policy > Contract management > Managing contracts through their lifecycle > Variation and renewal

- Any modification to the scope, value, or terms of a contract is a variation, initiated by the End-User. A variation of 20% or less is endorsed by the Procurement Manager; a variation above 20% MUST be submitted to the Procurement Committee, both prior to final DOA approval. - Renewals or extensions shall not be automatic and MUST be planned; End-Users submit a formal renewal request for Procurement Committee approval before any renewal process begins.

Procurement Policy > Contract management > Managing contracts through their lifecycle > Disputes and termination

- Minor disputes — slight scope deviations, timeline delays, or minor performance issues, resolved by the Procurement Department with the supplier and End-User to avoid escalation. - Major disputes — unethical or fraudulent practices, significant scope or timeline deviations, or severe performance failures, managed by the Procurement Department with the Legal Department. - Resolution options — invoice deductions or retentions, forfeiture of performance guarantees, liquidated damages (major, where permitted), claims against insurance or guarantees, contract termination, and legal action. - Termination — supported by documented justification, coordinated with the Legal Department, approved by the Procurement Committee, and finalized per the DOA based on contract value.

Procurement Policy > Vendor management > Registering, evaluating, and classifying vendors > Registration and performance

- All vendors MUST register through Nebras’s Vendor Registration Portal or Digital Procurement System; Procurement reviews company formation documents while Finance validates banking information. - Nebras maintains a centralized vendor master file; vendor status is actively monitored and may be deactivated for expired licenses or prolonged inactivity. - End-Users evaluate performance at Goods Receipt or Service Entry; the Procurement Department conducts quarterly reviews and initiates improvement plans where necessary. - Suspension or blacklisting may apply for contract breaches, safety violations, unethical conduct, or repeated performance failures; reactivation requires formal approval and reassessment.

Procurement Policy > Vendor management > Registering, evaluating, and classifying vendors > Vendor classifications

- Level 1 — Strategic — key partners and Critical Service Providers (CSPs) providing high-value, high-risk services or products critical to operations. - Level 2 — Operational — suppliers supporting core operations with medium-value, moderate-risk offerings where alternatives exist and disruption has limited impact. - Level 3 — Transactional — suppliers of low-value, low-risk goods or services that are easily replaceable. For onboarding strategic vendors and CSPs delivering high-risk, high-value goods or services, Third Party Risk Management (TPRM) applies: Information Security, IT, Finance, Risk, and Operations each provide risk mitigation questionnaires as part of prequalification, and the Procurement Committee ensures all CSPs are thoroughly assessed and endorsed by the respective departments.

Procurement Policy > Records & maintenance > Archiving, master data, and policy upkeep > Archiving and retention

- Procurement documents — contracts, purchase orders, tenders, and requisitions — shall be centrally archived with appropriate access controls. - Critical records shall be retained for a minimum of seven years, and other documents for at least three years, after which they are securely disposed of per applicable regulations.

chunks.text:
Procurement Policy > Records & maintenance > Archiving, master data, and policy upkeep > Master data and receipt

- Requests to create, modify, or extend material or service master records MUST be submitted to the Procurement Department with complete and accurate End-User details; asset codes remain the responsibility of the Finance Department. - End-Users MUST generate Goods Receipt Notes (GRNs) and Service Entry Sheets (SESs) in the Digital Procurement System promptly upon receipt, verifying deliveries and completing supplier performance evaluations to ensure timely vendor payments.

- The Procurement Department is responsible for maintaining and updating this policy. - Revisions are invalid unless authorized and formally approved per the authorities delegated by the Nebras Board of Managers, then communicated to all relevant departments.
